findings.normal_carrier_scope: Draft requires one column with 45 layers and exactly 32 positive native dry-mass values; it fills layers 1:32 from those host masses and derives layers 33:45 from the interface-pressure method.
findings.historical_driver_match: The pinned historical reference driver at lines 651-654 first assigns get_col_dry(h2o,plev*100) to all layers, then conditionally replaces only 1:n_native by native_dry_mass*avogad/(m_dry*10000). The draft uses exactly this split when the normal input has 32 native masses; it retains pressure-derived provenance for the replaced rows in its ledger.
findings.pressure_extension_match: The draft pressure expression follows the pinned frontend get_col_dry implementation at lines 1656-1661: absolute interface-pressure difference; fact=1/(1+H2O); m_air=(m_dry+m_h2o*H2O)*fact; then 10*deltaP*avogad*fact/(1000*m_air*100*g). Units follow the target driver convention of input PLEV in hPa and multiplying by 100 before get_col_dry.
findings.constants: The reference driver reads GRAVITY, CP_DRY, and MOL_WEIGHT_DRY and calls init_constants before get_col_dry (reference lines 317-325 for V8/V10; constants module lines 58-67). The draft reads GRAVITY and MOL_WEIGHT_DRY from the held packet and extracts the fixed m_h2o literal from the pinned constants source. The gas conversion is consistent with these initialized values.
findings.optics_path: Apart from the dry-column construction and single N2-absent normal case, the point calculation retains the reviewed v5 gas mapping, table order, interpolation state, major/minor indexing and term-ledger implementation. No optical-depth target is read by the locked function.
findings.required_execution_gate: Before any target opacity file is opened, the future runner must authenticate the normal V10 input and source pins and apply the already-required discrete pfrac context comparison. Pfrac is only a context cross-check; it must not supply opacity values. The draft itself remains locked and no such work was performed here.
findings.scope_limit: This establishes source-path consistency for the normal carrier only. It does not establish numerical agreement, coefficient-generation provenance, strict floating-point bounds, or physical accuracy.
